import pandas as pd

def main():
    # File paths for the source tables
    source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_51/test_0.csv"
    source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_51/test_1.csv"
    
    # Load Source 0: Student-level data
    df_students = pd.read_csv(source0_path)
    # Expected columns: ['Student ID', 'student_name', 'gender', 'grade', 'school_name', 'reading_score', 'math_score']
    
    # Load Source 1: School-level data
    df_schools = pd.read_csv(source1_path)
    # Expected columns: ['School ID', 'school_name', 'type', 'size', 'budget']
    
    # Join student data with school data on 'school_name'
    # This will add 'School ID', 'type', 'size', 'budget' columns to each student row
    df_merged = pd.merge(df_students, df_schools, on='school_name', how='left')
    
    # Reorder columns to match target schema:
    # ['Student ID', 'student_name', 'gender', 'grade', 'school_name', 'reading_score', 'math_score', 'School ID', 'type', 'size', 'budget']
    target_columns = ['Student ID', 'student_name', 'gender', 'grade', 'school_name', 
                      'reading_score', 'math_score', 'School ID', 'type', 'size', 'budget']
    
    df_target = df_merged[target_columns]
    
    # Enforce data types as per target schema
    df_target = df_target.astype({
        'Student ID': 'int64',
        'student_name': 'string',
        'gender': 'string',
        'grade': 'string',
        'school_name': 'string',
        'reading_score': 'int64',
        'math_score': 'int64',
        'School ID': 'Int64',  # Use nullable integer type in case of missing values
        'type': 'string',
        'size': 'Int64',
        'budget': 'Int64'
    })
    
    # Write the transformed data to the target CSV file
    output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_51/target_multisource_cot.csv"
    df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
